title: Web Design and Programming
description: Building websites and web applications: the Web and its protocols, web design principles and planning, HTML tags, tables, links and forms, CSS and page layout, JavaScript, and server-side programming with PHP and MySQL. Built from Prof S. O. Akinola's Web Design and Programming for Beginners (HTML, CSS, JavaScript and PHP) and the web protocols note in the course folder.

topics.title: The Web, Websites and Web Applications
topics.summary: The Internet is a global network of networks; the World Wide Web is an information system on it that uses HTML, HTTP and URLs. A website is a collection of related web pages, while a web application builds on a website and takes user input that affects back-end business logic through client, middle and data tiers. Network protocols such as TCP, IP, HTTP, DNS and FTP make it work.
subtopics: Web page, website and home page

topics.title: Web Design Principles and Planning
topics.summary: Web design covers how content is delivered through the Web: its content, usability, appearance and structure. Web pages are static or dynamic, sites are entertainment or informational, and design draws on markup, style sheets, client- and server-side scripting and databases. Accessibility, planning, responsive design and performance make a site effective.
subtopics: The basic aspects of web design

topics.title: HTML Tags, Tables and Links
topics.summary: HTML marks up the text of a web page with tags, or elements, that the browser interprets. Pages are written in a text editor and saved as HTML files. Basic tags structure the page, table tags arrange data in rows and cells, and anchor tags create links within a page, to other pages, to the wider Web and to email.
subtopics: Requirements for designing a web page
HTML document structure and basic tags
Tables: rows, cells, borders, spacing and padding
Page jumps and links to other pages

topics.title: HTML Forms
topics.summary: Forms collect data from visitors. The form tag's METHOD and ACTION attributes say how and where the data is sent, and input elements include text boxes, password boxes, radio buttons, check boxes, pop-up menus, text areas, hidden fields and submit and reset buttons.
subtopics: The FORM tag: METHOD and ACTION
Submit, reset, image and hidden inputs

topics.title: CSS and Page Layout
topics.summary: Cascading Style Sheets control how HTML elements look. A CSS rule has a selector and a declaration of property and value. Styles can be inline, internal (embedded) or external, and external style sheets are preferred for whole sites. Modern layout uses Flexbox and CSS Grid.
subtopics: Common properties: colour, fonts and links

topics.title: JavaScript
topics.summary: JavaScript is a client-side scripting language that makes web pages interactive. It has untyped variables with global or local scope, arithmetic and assignment operators, control structures, functions, events such as onclick and onsubmit, cookies, form validation and arrays.
subtopics: What JavaScript is and where it goes
Control structures: if, switch and loops

topics.title: PHP and MySQL
topics.summary: PHP is a loosely typed server-side scripting language whose variables begin with $. It has global, local and static variable scopes, constants, eight data types, control structures, functions, arrays, string and file handling, and connects to MySQL databases through MySQLi or PDO to create tables and insert and select data with SQL.
subtopics: What PHP is; tags and comments
Data types, control structures and functions
Connecting to MySQL with MySQLi or PDO
